text: It was 3:17 am, just the yeast and silence. Marisol slid the first loaves into the oven and saw that worn paperback, The Borrowers, in the wicker basket by the back door. Every Thursday for six weeks someone had brought it back here rather than the library two blocks over. No name, no card. Just the book, faintly smelling of rain and woodsmoke. But tonight, between pages 84 and 85, there was a folded note. Marisol wiped her floury hands and opened it. It read: "I can't make it to the library before closing. Please keep it another week. I like knowing it's warm." She looked at the basket and the tray of cinnamon rolls cooling on the rack. Chose the most iced. Wrapped it in wax paper, tucked the note back in the book, set both by the door. Then she flipped the sign to OPEN and started the coffee.
